O.outcome_detail: resource allocation, help-seeking, and co-creation of quality

cells.quote: The review describes emerging collaborative QRIS approaches citing Alston (2025), in which resource allocation can promote help-seeking and enable co-creation of quality between government agencies and ECEC providers; the authors recommend trialling and evaluation.
cells.note: The study text provided does not contain the QRIS claim reported in the wiki entry; quote reproduced from the entry as permitted.

cells.quote: Broadly, with exception of gender for which no reported significant associations were found, the studies report a significant association of demand on educator (indexed by younger child age, higher learning needs, greater disadvantage and minority status) with reduced interactional quality.
cells.note: Narrative review synthesis of the reviewed classroom-composition studies.

cells.quote: The results across studies converge on the conclusion that heterogeneity of class composition in each of these measures, potentially another index of demand on educator, is associated with poorer standard observed interactional quality.
cells.note: The review synthesizes studies across age, ability, disadvantage, and minority-status composition.

cells.quote: In studies comparing global measures with those examining individual child experiences within a ECEC group, prediction of child development outcomes is of higher effect size when the individual child experience is the focus (Burchinal et al., 2021; Jeon et al., 2022).
cells.note: The comparison concerns measurement approaches rather than an instructional treatment.
